_about: Audit record for destinations.summary — the one-line claim shown on every destination card and at the top of every destination page. Applied by scripts/audit_summaries.php. A destination appears here ONLY once a person has actually re-verified its claims against a published source on the date given. Anything absent from this file has NOT been re-verified and correctly renders no review date.
_method: Every summary was first triaged mechanically for checkable claims (numbers, currency amounts, percentages, years, and date-bound words such as 'now', 'new', 'record'). 47 of 85 summaries carry at least one. Those were then ranked by how badly a wrong claim would mislead a traveller — legal powers, tax rates and entry rules first — and verified from source in that order.

summaries.note: Flagged for review on the assumption that the two-tier Louvre pricing was stale. It is not. The Louvre raised admission for non-EEA visitors by 45%, from EUR 22 to EUR 32, effective 14 January 2026; EEA visitors continue to pay EUR 22 and Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein are exempt from the increase. Guided-group entry is EUR 28. The claim stands as written.
sources: Louvre to hike ticket prices by 45% for most non-EU visitors — Artforum
Louvre museum to hike entrance fee by 45% for non-European visitors — CNN

summaries.note: Highest-risk claim in the set, because it asserts a police power. Verified: amendments under the National Security Law effective 23 March 2026 empower police, immigration and customs officers to compel device passwords from any person, including foreign travellers and transit passengers; separate border powers took effect 30 March 2026 and apply regardless of whether national security is suspected. Refusal is a criminal offence carrying up to one year in prison and a HK$100,000 fine.
sources: Hong Kong's new border-search powers allow officers to compel device passwords — VisaHQ
New Hong Kong law lets border officers demand phone and laptop passwords — VisaHQ

summaries.note: The levy is the UK's first city-wide visitor levy and took effect on 24 July 2026, thirteen days before this audit, so 'just started' is correct rather than merely surviving. It is 5% of the accommodation cost, capped at five consecutive nights, and does not apply to bookings made before 1 October 2025.
sources: Edinburgh Visitor Levy comes into effect — City of Edinburgh Council
UK's first city-wide visitor levy comes into effect in Edinburgh

summaries.note: Verified: Las Vegas visitation fell 7.5% in 2025 to 38.5 million, roughly 3.1 million fewer visitors than the prior year and the sharpest decline since record-keeping began in 1970 outside the pandemic. Projections for 2026 are a partial recovery to about 40.1 million, so the summary describes a real and recent trough rather than a continuing collapse.
sources: Las Vegas tourism down 7.5% in 2025 with 38.5 million visitors — Las Vegas Sun
Las Vegas visitation falls 7.5 percent in 2025 — Las Vegas Review-Journal

summaries.note: The Acropolis daily cap of 20,000 with staggered hourly entry has been in force since September 2023, with a maximum of 3,000 admitted in the 08:00-09:00 hour. Heat closures during severe heatwaves are also real. Verified while writing the Athens risk report.
sources: Acropolis cap on daily visitors and staggered entry times — Euronews

summaries.note: Barcelona raised its nightly accommodation levy in April 2026 to roughly $10-17 for hotels and about $14 for holiday rentals, among the highest in Europe, and continues to restrict short-term rentals as part of its overtourism response. 'Doubled tourist tax' and 'Airbnb phase-out' both hold.
sources: Barcelona raises taxes to address overtourism

summaries.note: Hawaii's Green Fee (Act 96 / SB1396, signed 27 May 2025) took effect 1 January 2026, adding 0.75% to the transient accommodations tax and taking Oahu's combined lodging tax from about 18.0% to about 18.7%.
sources: Court decision allows Hawaii's Green Fee to take full effect — KHON2

summaries.note: Los Angeles transient occupancy tax is 14%; hotels in the tourism marketing district add 2% of room revenue; resort fees of roughly $20-30 a night are common at beach properties.
sources: US hotel stays cost more as bed taxes climb

summaries.note: Miami Beach resort fees average around $25 a night, with luxury properties commonly $40-50 and some above $60, on top of a 4% city resort tax, 3% county convention development tax and 6% Florida sales tax.
sources: Miami hotel and Airbnb fees — resort fees, parking, taxes

summaries.note: Epic Universe single-day tickets run $139-$199 for adults depending on date, and a 3-day park-to-park ticket including Epic Universe starts around $520.79.
sources: 2026 Epic Universe tickets now on sale — Disney Tourist Blog

summaries.note: Car break-ins are well down from the 2023 peak and falling further into 2026. The Tenderloin, roughly bounded by Market, Powell, Geary and Van Ness, accounts for around 31% of tourist-related crime reports despite covering under 2% of the city's area.
sources: San Francisco safety guide 2026 — neighbourhood scores and crime data

summaries.verdict: row added by migration; production summary unchanged
summaries.note: The lisbon-portugal ROW was only ever defined in database/seed.php, so a database built from migrations alone lacked it entirely — migration 046 adds it, ON CONFLICT (slug) DO NOTHING. Production DOES already have the row (confirmed 2026-08-06 by a read-only HTTP 200 on https://ruinmytrip.com/d/lisbon-portugal), and its summary is the researched editorial line published by publish_editorial.php, not the demo seeder text. So 046 is a no-op in production and the live summary is left exactly as it is. The city-tax summary written into 046 applies only where the row does not yet exist. The verified fact behind it: the Lisbon city tax doubled to EUR 4 per person per night in September 2024, has held at EUR 4 through 2026, and is capped at seven nights.
sources: Portugal tourist tax 2026: verified rates by region
